logicalBugs.explanation: A valid workspace picture appears immediately after upload, but the first settled refresh of General settings can show an empty picture and disable Remove.

rootCause.explanation: uploadWorkspacePicture updates logoFileId directly in workspaceRepository without invalidating the cached workspaceEntity. The client initially displays the returned upload URL, but refresh can hydrate the older cached workspace without the new logo; replacement can also try deleting an already deleted logo ID.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A valid workspace picture appears immediately after upload, but the first settled refresh of General settings can show an empty picture and disable Remove.

sourceBugs.name: Uploaded workspace picture disappears after the first refresh

reproductionPaths.expected: A successfully uploaded workspace picture remains visible and removable after refreshing General settings.
reproductionPaths.actual: The picture appears after upload, then the first settled refresh shows the empty picture placeholder with Remove disabled. The uploaded file remains stored, and a later refresh may restore its display.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > General with no workspace picture set.
Upload a valid square PNG or JPEG under 10 MB and confirm the picture appears with Remove enabled.
Refresh General settings and wait for the page to finish loading.
Observe the empty picture placeholder and disabled Remove control.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Replacing an existing logo repeatedly on the same General settings page can save the latest image but return an error and retain the previous preview.

sourceBugs.name: Workspace-logo replacement returns an error after saving the new image

reproductionPaths.expected: A supported logo replacement should return success and show the saved image. Deleting the previous logo must use its current identity.
reproductionPaths.actual: From a reload-verified working logo, the first replacement succeeds. A subsequent replacement on the same mounted page returns an error and retains the prior preview, although later workspace reads and reload reveal the latest image was committed.
reproSteps: Save a small genuine workspace-logo image in Settings > General and reload to verify it persists.
Replace it with a distinct valid image and confirm success.
Without leaving General, replace it again with another distinct valid image.
Observe the generic error toast and retained previous preview.
Reload and observe the newest replacement, showing that it was saved despite the error response.
Controls: repeated replacements from an empty baseline work; saving another workspace setting between replacements prevents the tested failure.

matchingGuidance.distinction: N01 covers a valid workspace logo disappearing on first reload. This entry requires replacing a reload-verified existing logo repeatedly on the same General page and receiving an error after the latest replacement committed.

logicalBugs.explanation: After an unsupported upload breaks the profile picture preview, a subsequent valid image saves successfully but the preview stays gray until reload or remount.

rootCause.explanation: ImageInput sets isPictureURLError on an image-load error and never clears it when pictureURI changes. A later successful upload remains behind the error placeholder in the same mounted component.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After an unsupported upload breaks the profile picture preview, a subsequent valid image saves successfully but the preview stays gray until reload or remount.

sourceBugs.name: Profile picture preview stays blank after a valid replacement following an invalid upload

reproductionPaths.expected: Uploading a valid replacement image refreshes the profile picture preview immediately, including after an earlier image failed to render.
reproductionPaths.actual: Following a plain-text picture upload, later valid PNG uploads leave the picture tile as a gray placeholder after the upload settles. Reloading the page or leaving Profile and returning displays the newly saved valid image. Valid-image-to-valid-image replacement works without a prior broken preview; no saved image is lost.
reproSteps: At a 390-by-844 viewport, open Settings > Profile and upload a valid square PNG under 10 MB. Confirm it appears.
Upload a small plain-text .txt file through the same picture control and observe the broken or gray placeholder preview.
Upload a different valid square PNG and wait for the upload to settle.
Observe that the preview remains gray instead of showing the valid replacement.
Reload the page, or leave Profile and return. Confirm that the new valid picture appears, demonstrating that it was saved.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After an invalid workspace-image upload, a later supported image saves but its preview stays blank in the mounted upload control.

sourceBugs.name: Valid workspace image leaves a blank preview after an invalid upload

reproductionPaths.expected: A successful valid image replacement should clear prior image-error state and display the newly saved workspace picture.
reproductionPaths.actual: After an invalid upload and a later supported valid upload, the valid image saves successfully but the same mounted picture control displays a blank placeholder. Navigating away and reopening settings restores the client preview.
reproSteps: Open Settings → General → Picture in a disposable workspace.
Upload an invalid image to put the preview into its error state.
Upload a supported genuine image and wait for the successful save.
Observe that the picture control still shows a blank placeholder despite the accepted valid replacement.

Navigate away and reopen settings to remount the control; observe the saved image preview recover. Do not rely on a first reload as the sole control because a separate workspace-cache issue can return stale references.

matchingGuidance.distinction: The existing reference covers profile-picture preview recovery after an invalid upload. This entry covers the workspace-logo entry point and successful later valid-image preview. Unsupported workspace-file acceptance and P2-8 server errors after replacement commit are distinct defects.

logicalBugs.explanation: The initial data-model visualization overlaps neighboring object cards, obscuring field and relationship rows and their expand controls.

rootCause.explanation: The diagram layout gives every object node a fixed 220x100 geometry in Dagre and React Flow even though the rendered card height grows with its field rows. Layout separation and Fit view use the short fixed rectangle, causing overlaps and clipped lower rows.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The initial data-model visualization overlaps neighboring object cards, obscuring field and relationship rows and their expand controls.

sourceBugs.name: Data-model diagram initially overlaps object cards and obscures their rows

reproductionPaths.expected: The initial diagram layout allocates enough space for each full object card so that its labels, fields, relationships, and expand controls remain visible.
reproductionPaths.actual: Tall object cards overlap neighboring cards on fresh desktop diagram loads. Lower rows and expand controls are obscured, and Fit view or zoom preserves the overlap. Dragging the covering card away reveals the hidden content. No stored data is lost.
reproSteps: At desktop width, open Settings > Data model and select Visualize data model without dragging any cards.
Inspect neighboring cards with enough fields or relationships to extend below their headers. Observe that another card covers lower rows or expand controls.
Use Fit view or zoom and observe that the overlap remains.
Drag the covering card into empty space and confirm that the previously hidden rows and controls become accessible.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Fitting the data-model diagram can leave the lower part of an object card outside the canvas, even though zooming out reveals the complete card.

sourceBugs.name: Data-model Fit view leaves lower object-card fields clipped

reproductionPaths.expected: The diagram’s Fit control should frame the full visible object cards within the canvas.
reproductionPaths.actual: At a desktop viewport, repeated Fit clicks leave the lowest card’s field rows below the canvas edge. The control keeps the same framing, while zooming out or using a taller canvas reveals the missing content.
reproSteps: Open Settings → Data model → Visualize at a desktop viewport such as 1440×1000. Use a diagram with a tall object card near its lower boundary; creating a fresh custom object or expanding an object’s fields can provide this layout.
Click the four-corners Fit control and inspect the lowest visible object card’s field rows at the canvas bottom.
Click Fit again. The card’s lower field rows remain clipped at the edge.
Control: zoom out once or increase the canvas height, and confirm the complete card is visible. Repeat after reopening Visualize.

matchingGuidance.relatedReferenceName: Data-model diagram initially overlaps object cards and obscures their rows
matchingGuidance.distinction: Both involve fixed graph-node dimensions and taller visible cards. N21 covers neighboring cards overlapping each other. This entry covers lower canvas-edge clipping after using Fit; overlapping neighboring cards alone is not sufficient. Workflow canvases use separate entry points.

logicalBugs.explanation: A saved TWD Currency field set to Full format and 2 decimals reopens with the settings intact, but its preview still shows “元 2,000” with no decimal places.

rootCause.explanation: CurrencyDisplay treats configured decimals as maximumFractionDigits through formatNumber, whose minimumFractionDigits is zero. Preview values ending in zeros omit the requested decimal places, including the TWD example.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A saved TWD Currency field set to Full format and 2 decimals reopens with the settings intact, but its preview still shows “元 2,000” with no decimal places.

sourceBugs.name: Currency field preview omits configured decimal places for TWD

reproductionPaths.expected: After saving and reopening a Currency field with Taiwanese dollar, Full format, and 2 decimals, the preview should show two decimal places; the visible helper example says “1000.00 for 2 decimals.”
reproductionPaths.actual: The reopened field displayed Taiwanese dollar, Full, and 2 in its settings, while the preview persistently showed “元 2,000” without a decimal point or trailing digits. The mismatch remained visible after waiting five seconds.
reproSteps: Load the supplied authenticated state for Tim Apple and open the app in the Apple workspace.
Open the workspace menu, choose Settings, then Data model.
Create a fresh custom object with a unique name and open its Fields page.
Choose New Field > Currency and enter a unique field name.
Set Default Value to Taiwanese dollar (TWD), Format to Full, and Number of decimals to 2.
Save the field, then select it from the object's Fields list to reopen its configuration.
Observe that the persisted settings show TWD, Full, and 2, while the visible preview shows “元 2,000” without decimal places; the helper says “E.g. 1000.00 for 2 decimals.”

reproductionPaths.explanation: Percentage field preview ignores Number of decimals set to 1

sourceBugs.name: Percentage field preview ignores Number of decimals set to 1

reproductionPaths.expected: Preview should show one decimal place, consistent with the visible help example '99.0% for 1 decimal'.
reproductionPaths.actual: Number of decimals shows 1 and help says '99.0% for 1 decimal', but the preview remains '200,000%' without a decimal place.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > Data model and create a fresh custom object with unique singular and plural names.
Choose New Field > Number and enter a unique field name.
Change Number type from Number to Percentage.
Click the Number of decimals plus button once to select 1.
Observe that the helper promises one decimal place, but the settled preview shows 200,000% without a decimal point or trailing zero.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry covers the Number field editor switched to Percentage with one decimal place; mo-60m-twenty-9 covers the Currency field editor with TWD, Full format, and two decimals. Both omit decimal padding in their previews, but the configured field types and entry points differ.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Plain Number fields omit trailing-zero padding despite their configured decimal count and explicit fixed-decimal helper example.

sourceBugs.name: Number format preview omits the requested trailing decimal zeros

reproductionPaths.expected: A Number field configured for two decimal places should display trailing zeros consistently with the helper example, such as 2,000.00 and 1,234.50.
reproductionPaths.actual: The two-decimal preview displays 2,000 beside a helper example 1000.00. Saved records display 2000 as 2,000 and 1234.5 as 1,234.5. Fractional rounding still works: 1234.567 displays 1,234.57.
reproSteps: Create a fresh custom object with a plain Number field.
Set Number of decimals to two using the supported integer setting and compare the fixed-decimal helper with the preview. Observe missing trailing .00.
Save and reopen settings to confirm the decimal setting persisted.
Create records with values 2000, 1234.5 and 1234.567. Observe missing zero padding for the first two but correct two-decimal rounding for the last.
Controls: zero-decimal preview agrees with its helper and Short formatting displays the shortened form as configured.

matchingGuidance.distinction: The existing Percentage reference and mo-60m-twenty-9 Currency/TWD reference share trailing-zero suppression in the formatter but cover their own field-type entry points. This entry covers plain Number configuration, preview and record display; correct fractional rounding is not classified as broken.

logicalBugs.explanation: Mobile skill instructions expansion hides Save and offers no visible way to return to the form

rootCause.explanation: FormAdvancedTextFieldInput disables its fullscreen close control on mobile, while the mobile Settings breadcrumb may render no return control. Expanding Skill Instructions therefore removes the normal form Save context without exposing a reachable exit from the fullscreen editor.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Mobile skill instructions expansion hides Save and offers no visible way to return to the form

sourceBugs.name: Mobile skill instructions expansion hides Save and offers no visible way to return to the form

reproductionPaths.expected: Expanding instructions should leave a usable way to return to the skill form and save the skill at 390px width.
reproductionPaths.actual: At 390px width, expanding Instructions covers the skill form, including Save, and shows no close or return control. Pressing Escape leaves the editor expanded.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > AI > Skills > New Skill.
Enter a unique skill name, description, and instructions without saving.
Set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels and collapse navigation if it is open.
Click the expansion icon at the top-right of Instructions.
Observe that Save and every close or return control are hidden. Press Escape and confirm the editor stays expanded.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Expanding saved Workspace Instructions at mobile width covers AI settings while hiding both the close button and return breadcrumb.

sourceBugs.name: Expanded Workspace Instructions offers no mobile return control

reproductionPaths.expected: The expanded Workspace Instructions editor provides a usable control to return to its containing AI settings at supported mobile widths.
reproductionPaths.actual: At 390px and 768px, the expanded editor has no visible close or return control. Escape and Expand navigation panel do not dismiss it. Both judges reproduced twice with previously persisted content. At 769px and desktop width the X closes it correctly. Saved text remains intact.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > AI > Overview and enter disposable Workspace Instructions.
Allow autosave to finish and reload to confirm the content persisted.
Set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels and expand Workspace Instructions without making further edits.
Observe that the fullscreen editor covers settings and its header contains no close or return control. Press Escape and try the navigation-drawer toggle; the editor remains expanded.
As controls, resize to 769px or desktop width, observe the X, and click it to return to inline AI settings.
Repeat at mobile width with another already-persisted value. Do not require loss of text or an inability to leave the application page entirely.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry covers Settings > AI > Overview > Workspace Instructions, an autosaved workspace-wide editor opened with already-persisted content. N49 covers Skill Instructions in the skill form, where expansion hides Save. Both share mobile close-button and Settings breadcrumb suppression; match the reported entry point. workflows-recovered-11 instead has a visible Back to Send Email link that fails to close a workflow Body editor.

logicalBugs.explanation: Object creation permits a singular API name up to 63 characters, but supported long names make generated relation fields exceed their own name limit and creation fails.

rootCause.explanation: Object-name validation permits the object API-name length in isolation, but generated morph relation field names append object-specific suffixes and are checked against the same field-name maximum. A valid long object name therefore produces an overlength generated relation name during create/rename.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Object creation permits a singular API name up to 63 characters, but supported long names make generated relation fields exceed their own name limit and creation fails.

sourceBugs.name: Allowed long singular object API names fail generated relation validation

reproductionPaths.expected: A singular object API name within the allowed 63-character maximum can be saved successfully, or the form enforces the actual supported limit before submission.
reproductionPaths.actual: Fresh object creations with 58-, 61-, and 63-character singular API names failed with a Related field index validation failed error and retained the form values. Shortening the singular API name to 57 characters allowed creation. A long display label alone can work when its generated API name is shorter; no existing objects were lost.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > Data model and choose Add object.
Enter valid unique singular and plural display names. Open the Advanced API-name settings.
Set the singular API name to a unique valid 63-character name and keep the plural API name valid and short.
Click Save and observe that object creation fails with a related field/index validation error.
Shorten only the singular API name to 57 characters and save again. Confirm the object is created.

reproductionPaths.explanation: With label and API-name synchronization enabled, renaming an existing custom object to a permitted long singular label generates an overlong related-field name and fails. The attempted rename remains a draft; a generic related-field validation error appears and reload restores the previous saved name.

sourceBugs.name: Renaming an object to an allowed long name fails related-field validation

reproductionPaths.expected: Renaming with names within the form’s allowed limit should succeed, or the form should explain and enforce the actual supported limit before generating invalid companion fields.
reproductionPaths.actual: With label and API-name synchronization enabled, renaming an existing custom object to a permitted long singular label generates an overlong related-field name and fails. The attempted rename remains a draft; a generic related-field validation error appears and reload restores the previous saved name.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, create a uniquely named custom object with short valid singular and plural names, then open its Settings.

Keep Synchronize Objects Labels and API Names enabled. Replace Singular with P2OBJ Boundary ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTU and blur the field. Its generated plural has 63 characters and its singular API name has 60.
Observe the related-field validation error and unchanged saved header. Reload and confirm the previous saved names remain.
Compare a shorter synchronized name, or disable synchronization while retaining short API names and enter the same long display labels; these save successfully.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry covers synchronized singular-label renaming of an existing custom object. The related N56 entry covers object creation with explicitly supplied long API names; creation adds no separate finding here.

logicalBugs.explanation: Sorting the AI Skills list by Type throws a Boolean localeCompare error and replaces the settings page content with an error screen.

rootCause.explanation: The Skills Type column declares the Boolean isCustom field as string. The shared sorter calls localeCompare on its Boolean value without conversion, throwing during list rendering.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Sorting the AI Skills list by Type throws a Boolean localeCompare error and replaces the settings page content with an error screen.

sourceBugs.name: Sorting Skills by Type crashes AI settings

reproductionPaths.expected: Clicking the supported Type sort header should reorder Skills while keeping the settings page usable.
reproductionPaths.actual: Clicking Type replaces the AI settings tabs and Skills list with Sorry, something went wrong and a Reload button. The Settings sidebar remains visible. Reload restores the list, and clicking Type crashes it again. Saved Skill content remains intact.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > AI > Skills in a workspace containing multiple Skills.
If needed, create a uniquely named custom Skill alongside the seeded Skills and save it.
Click the Name sort header and confirm the list remains usable; correct Name ordering is not required for this control.
Click the Type sort header and observe the settings page content replaced by the error screen.
Use Reload, reopen Skills if necessary, and click Type again to reproduce the crash.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Sorting the Companies Indexes table by Unique calls a string comparator on a Boolean and replaces Data model settings content with the page error display.

sourceBugs.name: Sorting Indexes by Unique crashes Data model settings

reproductionPaths.expected: Sorting indexes by the supported Unique column should reorder the table while keeping Data model settings usable.
reproductionPaths.actual: Clicking Unique replaces the breadcrumb, header, tabs and Indexes table with the page error display while the Settings sidebar remains visible. Reload restores the table. Type sorting works, and the same displayed index names and uniqueness flags remain after recovery.
reproSteps: As an administrator, open Settings > Data model > Companies.
Enable Advanced and open the Indexes section with multiple indexes.
Sort by Type and confirm the table remains usable.
Click Unique to sort the indexes and observe the settings content replaced by the error screen.
Reload, reopen Indexes and repeat the Unique sort to reproduce the crash.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry covers Settings > Data model > Indexes > Unique, using isUnique metadata. The related entry covers Settings > AI > Skills > Type, using isCustom metadata. Both reach the shared Boolean/string comparator mismatch through different table columns and entry points.

logicalBugs.explanation: Autosaving changed Instructions in a saved Skill remounts its editor, closing fullscreen and formatting menus and losing focus.

rootCause.explanation: The Skill and Workspace Instructions hosts use their last saved rich-text content as the editor React key. Successful autosave updates that key and remounts the shared editor, dropping focus and resetting fullscreen/menu state.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Autosaving changed Instructions in a saved Skill remounts its editor, closing fullscreen and formatting menus and losing focus.

sourceBugs.name: Saved Skill Instructions autosave remounts the editor and interrupts editing

reproductionPaths.expected: Autosaving Instructions should preserve the active editor, fullscreen state, focus and offered formatting menu so editing can continue.
reproductionPaths.actual: After editing expanded Instructions and pausing for autosave, the editor returns inline and loses focus. Continued typing without refocusing enters nothing. A slash-formatting menu also disappears after a changed value saves. Text entered before the remount persists through reload.
reproSteps: Create and save a uniquely named Skill with Instructions, then reopen it.
Expand Instructions, edit its content, and pause for autosave.
Observe the expanded editor close without a close action and lose focus. Attempt ordinary continued typing without refocusing; it enters nothing.
Reload and verify the text entered before the reset persisted.
Formatting variation: in a saved Skill, change Instructions and open the slash-command menu. Let the changed content autosave before choosing an option; the editor remounts and the menu disappears.
Controls: open saved Instructions without editing, or edit Instructions in an unsaved new-Skill form; the editor stays expanded. Sustained typing delays the reset until the debounce fires.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Successful Workspace Instructions autosave interrupts continued editing by closing the expanded editor or dropping compact-editor focus.

sourceBugs.name: Workspace Instructions autosave remounts the editor, closing fullscreen and dropping focus

reproductionPaths.expected: Autosave should preserve the editor’s focus and expanded state so the user can continue typing after a pause.
reproductionPaths.actual: After typing and pausing, completed autosave closes the expanded editor after about one second. In compact mode it drops focus, so a second typing burst after a four-second pause does not appear until the user clicks again. Text entered before the reset remains saved.
reproSteps: As workspace administrator, open Settings > AI > Overview and save Workspace Instructions.
Expand the saved instructions, type additional text and pause long enough for autosave. Observe the expanded editor closing without an explicit close action.
In the compact editor, click into the content, type, pause four seconds and type a second sentence without clicking again. Observe that focus was lost and the second sentence does not appear.
Confirm text entered before the reset survives reload. Compare an idle expanded editor and continuous typing, both of which preserve editing state.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry covers Workspace Instructions in AI Overview. The related reference covers saved Skill Instructions. Both remount after autosave; the mobile missing-exit cases and reload-before-autosave text persistence cases are separate.

logicalBugs.explanation: Immediately regenerating an API key with a finite expiration repeatedly shortens its saved lifetime by roughly one additional day each time.

rootCause.explanation: computeNewExpirationDate truncates the original lifetime to whole days with differenceInDays and adds that integer duration to the regeneration time. The sub-day portion of the original expiration interval is lost on regeneration.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Immediately regenerating an API key with a finite expiration repeatedly shortens its saved lifetime by roughly one additional day each time.

sourceBugs.name: Regenerating an API key shortens its saved expiration

reproductionPaths.expected: Regenerating an API key renews its configured expiration duration without cumulatively losing days.
reproductionPaths.actual: Each immediate regeneration moves the persisted expiration earlier by roughly another day. The shortened expiration survives reloading, while reloading without regeneration preserves it.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > MCP & APIs > API.
Create a disposable API key with a unique name, an available role, and a 15-day expiration. Save it and note its expiration.
Reload the key details, select Regenerate Key, enter yes, and confirm.
Reload the details and observe the shortened remaining lifetime.
Immediately regenerate the key again and reload. Observe another roughly one-day reduction rather than renewal of the original duration.

logicalBugs.explanation: Clearing an existing AI skill description appears to work, but reopening or refreshing the skill restores the previous description.

rootCause.explanation: SettingsSkillForm sends description: formValues.description || undefined for both update/save paths. Clearing a saved description becomes an omitted field rather than an explicit empty string, so the mutation leaves the previous description unchanged.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Clearing an existing AI skill description appears to work, but reopening or refreshing the skill restores the previous description.

sourceBugs.name: Clearing a saved AI skill description does not persist

reproductionPaths.expected: Removing an optional skill description persists after autosave, just like replacing it with another nonempty description.
reproductionPaths.actual: An empty or whitespace-only description is silently discarded. After waiting for autosave and reopening or refreshing the skill, the previous description returns; nonempty changes persist.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > AI > Skills and create a disposable skill with a unique name, nonempty description, and instructions. Save it.
Reopen the skill, clear its description completely, blur the field, and wait at least three seconds for autosave.
Return to the skills list and reopen the skill, or refresh its editor.
Observe that the previous description returns. Replacing the description with different nonempty text persists under the same steps.

logicalBugs.explanation: The workspace menu offers Invite user to members without invitation permission, but selecting it silently redirects to Profile instead of explaining that the action is unavailable.

rootCause.explanation: The Invite user navigation action is exposed independently of the WORKSPACE_MEMBERS setting permission required by the Members/Invite route. The settings route guard redirects unauthorized members to their permitted Profile page without an explanation at the source action.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The workspace menu offers Invite user to members without invitation permission, but selecting it silently redirects to Profile instead of explaining that the action is unavailable.

sourceBugs.name: Restricted members see an unusable Invite user action that silently redirects to Profile

reproductionPaths.expected: An invitation action unavailable to the current member is hidden or disabled, or explains the permission restriction when selected.
reproductionPaths.actual: Invite user appears as an available workspace-menu action for a restricted member. Selecting it closes the menu and leaves the member on Profile with no invitation form or permission explanation. Authorized administrators can still use the invitation flow.
reproSteps: Sign in as a workspace member who lacks permission to manage workspace members, and open Settings > Profile.
Open the navigation sidebar if it is collapsed, then open the workspace dropdown.
Select Invite user.
Observe that the dropdown closes and Profile is displayed without an invitation form or permission explanation.

logicalBugs.explanation: At a narrow browser width, ordinary mouse clicks on saved navigation folder contents fail to open their destinations until layout customization has been entered in the current session.

rootCause.explanation: Navigation folder contents are wrapped in sortable/draggable items while navigation is delegated through NavigationDrawerItem click/mousedown handlers and mobile collapse state. In a fresh narrow session the drag/navigation boundary can consume pointer clicks before item navigation; exact first-session event ordering is not established by static inspection.
rootCause.assessment: Source-informed hypothesis; exact state transition was not independently reproduced during this source-clustering pass.

reproductionPaths.explanation: At a narrow browser width, ordinary mouse clicks on saved navigation folder contents fail to open their destinations until layout customization has been entered in the current session.

sourceBugs.name: Mouse clicks on navigation folder contents fail in a fresh narrow-width session

reproductionPaths.expected: Clicking a saved navigation item with a mouse opens its configured destination at narrow widths, as it does at desktop widths.
reproductionPaths.actual: At a 390-by-844 viewport after reload, mouse clicks on folder contents neither navigate nor open a destination tab, and the folder panel remains open. Touch taps, desktop-width mouse clicks, and narrow-width top-level navigation items work. Entering and canceling layout customization temporarily restores the folder mouse clicks; reloading restores the failure.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator at desktop width, open Settings > Layout > Customize. Create and save a disposable navigation folder containing a custom link to the current application origin plus /settings/layout.
Confirm that clicking the saved link at desktop width opens Layout settings.
Resize the browser viewport to 390 by 844 pixels and reload. Do not enter layout customization after this reload.
Open workspace navigation, open the saved folder, and click its nested link with an ordinary stationary mouse click.
Observe that no destination opens and the folder panel remains visible. Repeat the click to confirm the failure.
Enter layout customization and cancel it, then retry the same folder link with the mouse. Observe that it now works; reload and repeat the narrow-width click to observe the failure again.

logicalBugs.explanation: After a displayed custom field is deactivated and reactivated, it is active in Data model settings but remains absent from saved record Fields layouts.

rootCause.explanation: activateMetadataField only updates isActive:true on field metadata. Deactivation has already removed/hidden the field from saved layout/view-field configuration, and activation does not recreate that placement, so the field becomes active without returning to its former record layout position.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After a displayed custom field is deactivated and reactivated, it is active in Data model settings but remains absent from saved record Fields layouts.

sourceBugs.name: Reactivating a custom field does not restore its record layout placement

reproductionPaths.expected: Reactivating a previously displayed custom field restores its placement in the record Fields section, including access to its existing value.
reproductionPaths.actual: The reactivated field is listed as active in settings but remains missing from the record Fields section and side panel after reload, while other visible fields remain. Manually adding the field back through Edit Layout restores it with its saved value, so the data has not been deleted.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, create a disposable custom object with a Multi-select field containing a Red option and another field to use as an unchanged control.
Create a record, set the Multi-select field to Red, and use a saved record Fields layout in which both the Multi-select and control fields are visible.
Deactivate the Multi-select field in Data model settings and confirm it disappears from the record while the control field remains visible.
Reopen the field settings and activate it again. Confirm it appears as active in the settings field list.
Reload the record page and reopen its side panel. Observe that the reactivated field remains absent from the Fields section.
Use Edit Layout to show the field again. Observe that the Red value returns and remains after reload.

logicalBugs.explanation: Select option labels that generate the same API value disable Save without showing the collision error, even when the visible labels differ.

rootCause.explanation: Select option API values are normalized from labels and the form schema rejects colliding normalized values. Save derives its disabled state from form validity, but the option row/API-value editor does not render the corresponding duplicate-value validation message beside the input.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Select option labels that generate the same API value disable Save without showing the collision error, even when the visible labels differ.

sourceBugs.name: Select option API-value collisions disable Save without explaining the error

reproductionPaths.expected: The field editor displays a validation error explaining the API-value collision while blocking the invalid save.
reproductionPaths.actual: Renaming an option to Ready! while another option is Ready generates the same internal value READY for both. Save becomes disabled without displaying the duplicate-value error. With Advanced settings off, the conflicting API values are hidden. Correcting the collision enables Save.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, create a disposable custom Select field with Draft and Ready options, and save it.
Reopen the field editor with Advanced settings off and rename Draft to Ready!.
Blur the option input. Observe that the distinct visible labels Ready! and Ready leave Save disabled without an explanation of the conflicting internal values.
Rename the changed option to a distinct value such as Done. Observe that Save becomes enabled and the valid options can be saved.

logicalBugs.explanation: A user granted Roles permission without Users permission can edit roles directly, but the Roles breadcrumb redirects to Profile and role-list navigation is absent.

rootCause.explanation: The standalone Roles route is protected by ROLES but redirects to the Members page #roles, whose enclosing route requires WORKSPACE_MEMBERS. Navigation only exposes Members under that latter permission, so a roles-only user can reach role details but not the Roles list.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A user granted Roles permission without Users permission can edit roles directly, but the Roles breadcrumb redirects to Profile and role-list navigation is absent.

sourceBugs.name: Roles-only permission allows role editing but cannot reach the Roles list

reproductionPaths.expected: A user permitted to manage roles can reach the Roles list and return to it from an allowed role editor without also needing permission to add or remove users.
reproductionPaths.actual: The role editor is accessible and role edits save, but its Roles breadcrumb and the Roles list route redirect to Profile. Members and Roles entries are absent from the settings sidebar. Enabling Users in addition to Roles restores the list and navigation; disabling Users restores the failure.
reproSteps: As an administrator, create a disposable role with Settings All Access off, Roles on, and Users plus other individual settings permissions off. Record an existing role editor link.
Assign the role to a secondary workspace member, then sign in as that member with the updated permissions.
Observe that the settings sidebar has no Members or Roles entry.
Open the recorded role editor link and confirm that the role editor is available and a description edit can be saved and retained after reload.
Click the Roles breadcrumb and observe that Profile opens instead of the Roles list.
As the administrator, enable only Users in addition to Roles for the same member role. Reload or sign in again as the member and verify that the Roles breadcrumb now opens the list.

logicalBugs.explanation: After the data model changes in a separate authenticated session, loading the app in another tab of the original session can reset its open valid field form and discard unsaved settings.

rootCause.explanation: Data-model configuration editors keep unsaved values in mounted React Hook Form instances initialized from metadata. Shared metadata refresh can replace the surrounding metadata-driven editor tree and recreate those instances from saved metadata without retaining dirty drafts. The specific remount trigger during the cross-tab reproduction remains source-inferred.
rootCause.assessment: Source-informed hypothesis; exact state transition was not independently reproduced during this source-clustering pass.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After the data model changes in a separate authenticated session, loading the app in another tab of the original session can reset its open valid field form and discard unsaved settings.

sourceBugs.name: Metadata refetch in another tab discards unsaved data-model forms

reproductionPaths.expected: Background metadata synchronization preserves valid unsaved field settings in an unchanged foreground tab.
reproductionPaths.actual: The foreground relation form loses its source name, inverse name and destination; a Text-field form loses its name. Save becomes disabled. Persisted records or saved settings are not deleted.

In browser session A, start a new relation field on the source, select the target and enter unique source and inverse names; leave this valid draft unsaved.

Open another tab in browser session A and load a normal app page, such as Companies, while keeping the original field form open.

logicalBugs.explanation: Saved comma-decimal number preferences are ignored by abbreviated currency amounts and aggregate summaries in Opportunities.

rootCause.explanation: CurrencyDisplay uses formatToShortNumber for the default short representation instead of the locale-aware useNumberFormat formatter. Abbreviated opportunity amounts therefore retain the short helper decimal separator regardless of the selected comma-decimal preference.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Saved comma-decimal number preferences are ignored by abbreviated currency amounts and aggregate summaries in Opportunities.

Open Settings > Experience and set Number format to Dots and comma, with example 1.234,56. Confirm the saved preference.
Open Opportunities and inspect the abbreviated Amount values and an Average or Sum summary containing a fractional abbreviated value.
Observe decimal points in the short amounts and summary rather than the selected decimal commas.
As a control, inspect a Full-format currency field containing the same amount and confirm that it follows the comma-decimal preference.

logicalBugs.explanation: Clicking a named object title in the data-model visualizer opens the overall object catalog instead of that object’s data-model details.

rootCause.explanation: The diagram object title builds its link with SettingsPath.Objects, the generic catalog route, while supplying an objectNamePlural parameter unused by that route. It should target the per-object detail route.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Clicking a named object title in the data-model visualizer opens the overall object catalog instead of that object’s data-model details.

Click an unobscured object title such as Companies. If another card covers it, drag the covering card away first.

logicalBugs.explanation: An API key configured to Never expires is displayed with a far-future calendar expiry in its role Assignment table.

rootCause.explanation: Role assignment displays every truthy API-key expiresAt with formatDateString. The API-key Never expires representation is a far-future timestamp, so this surface formats the sentinel as a real date rather than using the API-key expiration formatter.

reproductionPaths.explanation: An API key configured to Never expires is displayed with a far-future calendar expiry in its role Assignment table.

sourceBugs.name: Role Assignment shows a far-future date for Never expires API keys

reproductionPaths.actual: API key details show Never expires and the API key inventory shows Never, but the role’s Assigned API keys table renders a far-future calendar date in Expires, including after reload. This is a display inconsistency; no actual key-use failure or expiry loss was observed.

Create a disposable API key with expiration set to Never and assign it to that role, either during creation or through the role Assignment tab.

Open the role’s Assignment tab and locate the key under Assigned API keys.

logicalBugs.explanation: The layout editor accepts a URL containing spaces and no valid hostname, publishing an unusable workspace navigation link.

rootCause.explanation: Navigation link editing trims and applies ensureAbsoluteUrl but does not validate the resulting URL against a hostname/URL schema. Malformed text can therefore be saved as a link and opened by the regular external-link control.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The layout editor accepts a URL containing spaces and no valid hostname, publishing an unusable workspace navigation link.

sourceBugs.name: Navigation layout saves malformed link URLs that open a browser error page

reproductionPaths.expected: Saving a navigation link rejects malformed URLs and explains how to correct the value.
reproductionPaths.actual: Saving this is not a url succeeds without validation and stores https://this is not a url. The malformed link survives reload and opens a browser error tab when clicked. Valid URL controls save and open successfully through the same flow.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, open Settings > Layout > Customize and choose Add menu item > Link.

Blur the URL field, save the link, publish the layout, and reload.

Click the link and observe a browser error tab. As a control, create a link to https://example.org through the same flow and confirm that it opens successfully.

logicalBugs.explanation: After editing an object’s API name, existing indexes lose their field labels and cannot be found by field-name search. New index creation can intermittently cause the same display and search failure.

rootCause.explanation: Index labels are reconstructed by matching indexField.fieldMetadataId to the current object fields. Object API-name mutation metadata can leave stale index-field IDs in the client object/index projection, so the unmatched entries are filtered out and the labels and label-based search become empty until consistent metadata is loaded.
rootCause.assessment: Source-informed hypothesis; exact state transition was not independently reproduced during this source-clustering pass.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After editing an object’s API name, existing indexes lose their field labels and cannot be found by field-name search. New index creation can intermittently cause the same display and search failure.

sourceBugs.name: Object API-name edits leave indexes without field labels or field-name search

reproductionPaths.expected: Saved indexes retain their field labels and remain searchable by those field names after object API-name edits and index creation.
reproductionPaths.actual: Existing BTREE and GIN rows can show blank Fields cells after an object API-name edit. Searching Name returns no matching indexes, while searching BTREE still finds the unlabeled index. New index creation intermittently produces the same blank-label and failed-field-search state. Reload restored the labels and search in observed cases, though some reloads retained the incomplete display. No stored-index loss was observed.
reproSteps: As a workspace administrator, create a disposable custom object, enable Advanced settings, and add a Name BTREE index.
Open the object’s Indexes list and verify that the Name field label appears and searching Name finds its index.
Edit and save the object’s singular API name, disabling label/API-name synchronization if necessary, then return to the Indexes list.
Observe blank Fields labels on existing indexes. Search Name and observe no matching indexes; search BTREE and confirm that the unlabeled row is still present.
Reload and compare the labels and field-name search. Reload can restore the missing metadata, although recovery was not consistent across all attempts.
For the intermittent creation variant, repeat adding a Name index on fresh custom objects and inspect its field label and field-name search immediately after saving.

logicalBugs.explanation: At phone and tablet widths, closing a navigation customization panel leaves subsequent folder and link editors without their editing controls.

rootCause.explanation: Side-panel close clears selectedNavigationMenuItemIdInEditModeState, while the narrow-layout close/reopen transition also reuses that same selection for editing. A late close/reset can clear the newly selected folder/link, and SidePanelNavigationMenuItemEditPage renders its empty selection placeholder. Exact effect ordering is inferred from the reported narrow-only transition.
rootCause.assessment: Source-informed hypothesis; exact state transition was not independently reproduced during this source-clustering pass.

reproductionPaths.explanation: At phone and tablet widths, closing a navigation customization panel leaves subsequent folder and link editors without their editing controls.

sourceBugs.name: Navigation folder and link editors become empty after a mobile or tablet panel close

reproductionPaths.expected: Selecting a saved navigation folder or link displays its editing controls each time the editor is opened, including after another panel has been closed.
reproductionPaths.actual: At 390-by-844 and 768-by-1000, the first selection on a fresh page works. After closing a panel and selecting a folder or link again, its editor shows only Select a navigation item to edit and a close control. The folder/link settings are unavailable. Desktop close-and-reopen controls work, and saved navigation items remain intact.
reproSteps: At desktop width, create and save a disposable navigation folder with a nested link in Settings > Layout > Customize.
At a 390-by-844 or 768-by-1000 viewport, open layout customization on a fresh page and select a navigation item. Confirm that the initial editor shows its controls.
Close that panel, then select the saved folder again.
Observe that Edit folder contains only Select a navigation item to edit rather than its editing controls.
Close the panel and select the nested link; observe the same empty Edit link state. Compare with working close-and-reopen controls at desktop width.

logicalBugs.explanation: A multi-destination relation saved as Belongs to one reopens with Has many in its editor selector and preview, while the Relations list retains the correct saved type.

rootCause.explanation: SettingsDataModelFieldRelationForm initializes relationType only from existingFieldMetadataItem.relation?.type, then defaults to ONE_TO_MANY. Multi-destination fields store their relation legs in morphRelations instead, so their saved MANY_TO_ONE choice is ignored on reopen.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A multi-destination relation saved as Belongs to one reopens with Has many in its editor selector and preview, while the Relations list retains the correct saved type.

sourceBugs.name: Saved multi-destination Belongs to one relation reopens as Has many

reproductionPaths.expected: The saved relation editor displays Belongs to one, matching the chosen type, stored relation, and Relations list.
reproductionPaths.actual: After saving a Belongs to one relation with two destination objects, the refreshed Relations list says Belongs to one, but reopening the editor shows Has many in both selector and preview. Description saves preserve the stored MANY_TO_ONE relation. Single-destination Belongs to one reopens correctly; no record-linking failure or data loss was demonstrated.
reproSteps: Create three disposable custom objects in Settings > Data model.
On the source object, add a relation targeting the other two objects and provide the required inverse field name.
Choose Belongs to one and save.
Reload and confirm that the Relations list says Belongs to one.
Open the relation editor and observe Has many in its relation-type selector and preview.
As a control, create a single-destination Belongs to one relation and confirm that its editor retains the correct type.

logicalBugs.explanation: Reset to default restores all Address subfields in the preview but the reset is omitted from saving, so reopening or refreshing retains the previously saved custom selection.

rootCause.explanation: Address Reset to default uses resetField with a new defaultValue for settings.subFields. That changes the field baseline instead of marking an explicit user edit dirty, so canSave can remain false and the reset is not persisted.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Reset to default restores all Address subfields in the preview but the reset is omitted from saving, so reopening or refreshing retains the previously saved custom selection.

sourceBugs.name: Address Sub-Fields Reset to default does not save or persist

reproductionPaths.expected: Reset to default followed by Save persists the restored default Address subfield selection, just as manually restoring the same checkboxes does.
reproductionPaths.actual: After a saved Address field has four or five selected subfields, Reset to default displays Default and all six in the preview. Uncheck one or two Address subfields, save, and reopen to confirm the custom selection persists.
Open Sub-Fields and select Reset to default. Observe Default and all six subfields in the preview.
Click the enabled Save button and wait. Observe that the editor remains open, then refresh and confirm that the old custom selection returns.
For a successful-save variation, reset again, change the description, and click Save. Reopen the field and observe that the description persisted but the subfield reset did not.
As a control, manually check the previously omitted subfields, click Save, and reopen. Confirm that all six subfields persist.

logicalBugs.explanation: Saving one multi-destination relation displays multiple identical whole-relation rows until the page is refreshed.

rootCause.explanation: A morph relation is represented by multiple per-destination field metadata records. Mutation draft application appends those rows directly to the metadata store, while full metadata hydration collapses them into one logical field. The Relations table therefore renders one duplicate per destination until refetch normalizes the representation.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Saving one multi-destination relation displays multiple identical whole-relation rows until the page is refreshed.

sourceBugs.name: Creating a multi-destination relation shows duplicate rows until refresh

reproductionPaths.expected: One newly saved multi-destination relation appears as one row representing all its destinations, immediately after Save as well as after refresh.
reproductionPaths.actual: A single Save for a relation with two destination objects produces two identical rows in the Relations list. Refresh collapses them to one. A three-destination variation produces three rows then one. Single-destination controls stay at one row. The duplicate rows open working editors; no duplicate stored data, record-linking failure, or data loss was demonstrated.
reproSteps: Create three disposable custom objects in Settings > Data model.
On the source object, add one relation targeting the other two objects, enter the required inverse field name, and choose Belongs to one.
Click Save once and inspect the Relations list without refreshing.
Observe two identical rows representing that same relation and its two destinations.
Refresh and observe that the rows collapse to one. As a control, create a single-destination relation and confirm that it stays at one row.

logicalBugs.explanation: After a duplicate field label or API-name rename is rejected, the editor can switch to the conflicting field while retaining the original field URL. Subsequent corrected Save or Delete then affects that other field.

rootCause.explanation: SettingsObjectFieldEdit sets newNameDuringSave before awaiting the rename and resolves the current field by either the original name or that pending name. A rejected duplicate rename leaves the pending name set, so find can select the other existing field and subsequent edits/delete act on its ID.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After a duplicate field label or API-name rename is rejected, the editor can switch to the conflicting field while retaining the original field URL. Subsequent corrected Save or Delete then affects that other field.

sourceBugs.name: Rejected duplicate field rename retargets the editor and later edits or deletion to another field

reproductionPaths.expected: A rejected duplicate rename leaves the editor and its actions bound to the original field. Correcting or deleting that field must not mutate the unrelated conflicting field.
reproductionPaths.actual: When the conflicting field precedes the original in loaded metadata order, the rejected rename leaves the original URL but switches the header or type controls to the conflicting field. A corrected Save renames that other field, and Delete can remove it while preserving the original. Reload clears the switched state. Wrong-field schema mutations were observed; populated-record value loss was not tested.
reproSteps: On a disposable custom object, create a Text field Code and a Rating field Score. The failure is order-dependent: the conflicting field must precede the original field in loaded metadata order.
Open Score, leave label/API-name synchronization enabled, change its label to Code, and click Save.
Observe the duplicate-name error, then inspect the editor: the URL still identifies Score while controls have switched to the existing Text field.
Without reopening the editor, correct the label to a fresh unique name such as Quality and click Save.
Reload the field list and confirm that the original Text Code field became Quality while Rating Score remained unchanged.
On a separate disposable pair showing the same switch, inspect the Delete confirmation and confirm only in test data; the conflicting field is removed while the original remains.

logicalBugs.explanation: A custom object’s Record image setting cannot persist clearing a previously selected Files field to None, even after the automatic update request completes.

rootCause.explanation: The reported successful mutation returns the previous identifier despite the form submitting null, locating the failure on the nullable object-metadata update/override boundary. Pinned source explicitly retains null overrides in computeMetadataOverridesBlob and resolves them in getEffectiveImageIdentifierFieldMetadataId; a deterministic source defect explaining this report is not established. Do not conflate this with the independently confirmed metadata-event null-override display bug.
rootCause.assessment: Unresolved source cause: the source boundary is identified, but available evidence does not establish the distinct underlying defect.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A custom object’s Record image setting cannot persist clearing a previously selected Files field to None, even after the automatic update request completes.

sourceBugs.name: Clearing a Files-based Record image to None reverts after refresh

reproductionPaths.expected: Choosing None clears the custom object’s Record image setting and remains None after the save completes and the settings are reloaded.
reproductionPaths.actual: The dropdown shows None and submits an update with a null image identifier. The completed successful response still returns the previous field identifier, and a later metadata read and reload restore that old Files selection. Choosing or switching between non-null Files fields persists correctly. No image-file deletion or record-data loss was demonstrated.
reproSteps: Create a disposable custom object and a Files field such as Attachments.
In the object Settings tab, select Attachments as Record image and reload to confirm that it persisted.
Choose None. This control submits automatically; observe None in the dropdown.
Allow the update request to finish before refreshing. In the reproduced trial, a three-second wait captured a successful completed response that still returned the old image-field identifier.
Reload the settings and observe that Attachments returns rather than None.
As a control, select a different Files field, wait for the automatic update to complete, and reload to confirm that switching non-null selections persists.

logicalBugs.explanation: Approved-domain duplicate validation compares domain text case-sensitively, so changing capitalization allows separate saved registrations of the same domain.

rootCause.explanation: Approved domains are submitted/stored as the entered string without a common lowercase canonicalization before uniqueness comparison. Case-sensitive comparison therefore permits domains differing only by case.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Approved-domain duplicate validation compares domain text case-sensitively, so changing capitalization allows separate saved registrations of the same domain.

sourceBugs.name: Approved Domains accepts case-only duplicates

reproductionPaths.expected: An existing approved domain cannot be registered again by changing only ASCII letter case. The case-equivalent input is normalized or rejected as already registered.

Register a fresh lowercase domain such as qa-domain.example.test with a valid verification email prefix and save.

Change only the domain’s capitalization, such as QA-DOMAIN.EXAMPLE.TEST, and save.
Reload the Invite page and observe that both case-equivalent domains remain as separate Pending registrations.

logicalBugs.explanation: Disabling member applicability for an already assigned custom role makes the member’s Permissions role selector display a different role, although the original assignment remains intact.

rootCause.explanation: The member role selector filters out roles that can no longer be assigned to users. Its saved current role is absent from the remaining options, and the Select presentation falls back to the first eligible option instead of representing the still-assigned ineligible role; this changes the label without changing assignment.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Disabling member applicability for an already assigned custom role makes the member’s Permissions role selector display a different role, although the original assignment remains intact.

reproductionPaths.expected: The member’s Role selector displays the actual assigned role even when that role is no longer eligible for new member assignments.

Re-enable member applicability and reopen the member’s Permissions tab; the correct role name returns.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Disabling API-key applicability on an already assigned custom role makes the API-key editor display a different role, while the saved role assignment remains unchanged.

sourceBugs.name: API-key editor displays an unrelated role after API-key applicability is disabled

reproductionPaths.expected: The API-key editor displays the key’s actual assigned role even when that role is no longer eligible for new API-key assignments.
reproductionPaths.actual: After Assignable to API Keys is disabled and saved on the assigned role, the key editor displays the first remaining eligible role, such as Admin or an unrelated custom role. logicalBugs.explanation: Disabling and re-enabling an AI tool trigger replaces its inferred parameter schema with an empty schema despite unchanged typed function code.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Disabling and re-enabling an AI tool trigger replaces its inferred parameter schema with an empty schema despite unchanged typed function code.

logicalBugs.explanation: Removing a saved sidebar folder or folder child can select an adjacent external link and route its path on Twenty’s origin, displaying Page Not Found.

rootCause.explanation: The navigation-editor removal/adjacent-selection path routes the selected sibling through internal app navigation, even when it is an external link. Router path handling drops/reinterprets the external origin, unlike the normal link display which opens the complete URL externally.
rootCause.assessment: Source-informed hypothesis; exact state transition was not independently reproduced during this source-clustering pass.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Removing a saved sidebar folder or folder child can select an adjacent external link and route its path on Twenty’s origin, displaying Page Not Found.

sourceBugs.name: Removing a sidebar folder or child link routes an adjacent external link on the app origin

reproductionPaths.expected: Removing a sidebar folder leaves usable app content. If the next selected item is an external link, its configured origin is preserved and it is handled as an external destination.
reproductionPaths.actual: When the next selected sibling is an external link, removing the folder navigates to that link’s path, query and fragment on Twenty’s origin and displays Off the beaten path / Page Not Found. The saved link URL retains its external origin, and ordinary link clicks open the full external URL correctly in a new tab. logicalBugs.explanation: Editing Workspace Instructions and immediately opening Skills loses the edit without a save prompt or warning. Returning to Overview restores the previous instructions.

rootCause.explanation: Workspace Instructions uses a debounced update in SettingsAiOverviewTab without flushing it on tab unmount. Immediate AI-tab navigation disposes the pending callback before it saves the entered content.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Editing Workspace Instructions and immediately opening Skills loses the edit without a save prompt or warning. Returning to Overview restores the previous instructions.

sourceBugs.name: Workspace instruction edits are silently discarded when switching AI tabs

reproductionPaths.expected: The latest instructions should be saved when leaving the editor, or the app should warn that unsaved changes will be lost.
reproductionPaths.actual: The editor shows 'QA saved instruction one'; the new instructions are silently lost. Reproduced through Playwright fill followed by an ordinary Skills tab click, with no reload or forced navigation.
reproSteps: Open Settings > AI > Overview and save unique Workspace Instructions, waiting for the initial value to persist.
Replace the instructions and immediately use the ordinary Skills tab.
Return to Overview and reload. Observe the previous saved text instead of the replacement, without an unsaved-change warning.
Compare waiting beyond the one-second autosave debounce before switching tabs.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry loses pending text on ordinary tab navigation; the related entry preserves entered text but interrupts focus/fullscreen after autosave.

logicalBugs.explanation: When a Select field has a default option, saving any change to its options in Settings > Data model (even renaming an unrelated option) sets every record whose value was empty (null) to the default option. Data the user never touched is silently changed.

rootCause.explanation: Select option migration recreates the enum column with its configured default and copies only non-null old values. Existing NULL records are not copied and therefore acquire that default when any option edit rebuilds the column.

reproductionPaths.explanation: When a Select field has a default option, saving any change to its options in Settings > Data model (even renaming an unrelated option) sets every record whose value was empty (null) to the default option. Data the user never touched is silently changed.

sourceBugs.name: Editing any select field option overwrites empty record values with the field's default option

reproductionPaths.expected: Records whose select value is empty stay empty. Only records using the renamed option should change to the new value.
reproductionPaths.actual: After renaming the unrelated option 'Red' to 'Crimson' (no record used Red), record W3null went from null to 'LIME' (the default option). W4blue (BLUE_SKY) was unchanged. Earlier, renaming the default option Green to Lime also turned W1, which was empty before, into LIME.
reproSteps: Create a custom object with a nullable Select field, multiple options, and a configured default.
Create a record with an explicit null Select value and another using a nondefault option. The original report used the supported REST API for this setup.
Confirm the null value before editing field options. Rename an unused option through Settings > Data model and Save.
Read the records again and inspect the list. Observe the previously null value replaced by the default while the nondefault record retains its selection.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry fills existing null values with a default after an option edit; the related entry erases selected values after a corrected bulk-label typo.

logicalBugs.explanation: After UI deactivation and reactivation, a custom object’s Search section stays enabled but omits the indexed-field names, static weights and data types until full reload.

rootCause.explanation: Object reactivation writes the mutation response directly as FlatObjectMetadataItem into the metadata store, while the full hydration mapper normalizes search/index field metadata. Search information resolves through canonical metadata, so the differently shaped immediate response can temporarily omit its indexed fields until a full reload.
rootCause.assessment: Source-informed hypothesis; exact state transition was not independently reproduced during this source-clustering pass.

reproductionPaths.explanation: After UI deactivation and reactivation, a custom object’s Search section stays enabled but omits the indexed-field names, static weights and data types until full reload.

sourceBugs.name: Reactivating a custom object hides its Search information table until reload

reproductionPaths.expected: Reactivation should restore the saved Search information table consistently with the object’s enabled search configuration.
reproductionPaths.actual: The Name/Weight/Data type rows are present before deactivation, absent after reactivation and a ten-second wait, and restored after full reload. The weight is displayed information, not an editable control.
reproSteps: Enable Advanced settings and create a disposable custom object with its default Name field.
Open its Settings tab and confirm Global search is enabled and the Search table displays Name with weight 1.
Deactivate the object, then activate it through its Inactive Object Options menu in Data model.
Reopen its Settings tab and wait at least ten seconds. Observe the Search table rows remain missing while Global search is enabled.
Reload and reopen Settings; observe the Search information rows return.

matchingGuidance.distinction: Match the Search information table disappearing after custom-object reactivation and recovering on reload. Do not claim editable weight controls, changed ranking, lost saved configuration or failed global-search queries. Field reactivation failing to restore record-layout placement is a separate entry.

logicalBugs.explanation: Profile names autosave only after a delay. Navigating to another settings page immediately after editing cancels the pending change without saving or warning.

rootCause.explanation: NameFields schedules valid autosave through a 500ms debounce and returns debouncedUpdate.cancel from effect cleanup. Navigating away before the callback fires cancels the mutation instead of flushing the latest name.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Profile names autosave only after a delay. Navigating to another settings page immediately after editing cancels the pending change without saving or warning.

sourceBugs.name: Profile name edits are silently lost when navigating away

reproductionPaths.expected: Leaving the page should flush the pending profile update, or warn before discarding it.
reproductionPaths.actual: The updated name disappears and the original name returns. No save action, pending-save indicator, or unsaved-change warning protects the edit.
reproSteps: Open Settings > Profile with valid nonempty first and last names.
Replace First Name with a distinct nonempty value, then immediately click Data model in the settings sidebar.
Return to Profile and observe that the original name returns.
Control: wait on Profile after editing before navigating; the new name persists.

matchingGuidance.distinction: The related severity-1 entry covers missing feedback when an empty required Last Name is intentionally not saved. This severity-3 entry uses a valid nonempty name and ordinary navigation, which cancels its pending autosave. It does not require allowing empty names.
matchingGuidance.boundaries: Require the valid edit, ordinary settings navigation during the pending debounce, and restored old name on return, with a waited-save control. Do not match hard-refresh interruptions, clearing a required name, or a completed save later being overwritten. The missing-feedback-only and valid-edit-loss claims remain distinct.

logicalBugs.explanation: The permanent-erasure retention-days input in Settings Security has no accessible name.

rootCause.explanation: SettingsOptionCardContentCounter renders its title as ordinary text separate from SettingsCounter. It passes value/change bounds but no aria-label, labelledby or connected label ID to the underlying retention input, leaving the erasure field without an accessible name.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The permanent-erasure retention-days input in Settings Security has no accessible name.

sourceBugs.name: Permanent-erasure retention input has no accessible label

reproductionPaths.expected: Give the retention-days input an accessible name identifying Erasure of soft-deleted records and associate its description.
reproductionPaths.actual: The input is exposed as an unnamed textbox with value 14, without a label association, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title or placeholder. The report cites two axe audits and an accessibility snapshot.
reproSteps: Open Settings, General, then Security.
Find Other, Erasure of soft-deleted records.
Inspect the accessibility tree or navigate form fields with a screen reader; observe the unnamed retention-days textbox.
Run an accessibility audit and inspect the missing-label finding.

matchingGuidance.distinction: Missing accessible name for the permanent-erasure retention-days input; no edit or save failure is claimed.

logicalBugs.explanation: In the default light theme, Settings descriptions and sidebar section labels have insufficient text contrast.

rootCause.explanation: Settings card descriptions use font.color.light and sidebar section titles use font.color.tertiary on the light backgrounds without sufficient contrast for their small normal-weight text. These shared theme tokens produce the observed #999/#b3b3b3 foreground colors.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In the default light theme, Settings descriptions and sidebar section labels have insufficient text contrast.

sourceBugs.name: Settings descriptions and sidebar section labels have insufficient contrast

reproductionPaths.expected: Non-disabled small text should meet the 4.5:1 contrast threshold cited by the audit.
reproductionPaths.actual: Security descriptions use #999999 on white, reported as 2.84:1 contrast. User, Workspace and Other sidebar section labels use #b3b3b3 on #f9f9f9, reported as 1.99:1. Repeated axe audits flag these normal-weight small text labels.
reproSteps: Use the default light theme and open Settings, General, then Security.
Inspect the descriptions and User, Workspace and Other sidebar section labels.
Run a contrast audit and inspect the reported 2.84:1 and 1.99:1 failures.

matchingGuidance.distinction: Low contrast in active Settings descriptions and sidebar section labels under the default light theme; no functional failure is claimed.

logicalBugs.explanation: A valid pending Workspace name edit is lost when the user immediately switches from General to Security settings.

rootCause.explanation: NameField debounces workspace-name persistence for 500ms and returns debouncedUpdate.cancel from its effect cleanup. Switching away immediately cancels the pending save, discarding the local name edit.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A valid pending Workspace name edit is lost when the user immediately switches from General to Security settings.

sourceBugs.name: Workspace name edit is silently discarded when switching tabs immediately

reproductionPaths.expected: Normal settings navigation should flush the pending valid name save or warn before losing the edit.
reproductionPaths.actual: The name reverts without warning after switching General to Security and returning. The report reproduces it twice, with fill and character-by-character typing; waiting before navigation allows persistence.
reproSteps: Open Settings, General, then General and note the current workspace Name.
Enter a valid nonempty replacement name.
Immediately switch to Security, then return to General.
Observe the previous name restored without warning. Compare waiting after editing before switching tabs.

matchingGuidance.distinction: Covers Workspace Name in General settings with a General-to-Security tab switch. The related Profile entry covers Profile name during normal settings navigation; native-twenty-u17 covers AI Workspace Instructions.
